successors.note: The Kamerun page puts the German protectorate on 17 August 1884; the Cliopatria German Africa row starts in 1871 and grows only in 1885.

capitals.name: Kamerun (Cameroons Town, now Douala)
capitals.note: Not a seat of government: the dot marks the Duala area where the Hamburg firm C. Woermann opened the first German trading post in 1868 (Kamerun page). The Douala page says 'the town was also known as Cameroons Town' before 1884 and that 'the city known as Kamerun was renamed Douala' in 1885; the coordinates are the Natural Earth place Douala.

keyframe_review.note: 1,897.5 km2 for 1868-1869: a patch of about 56 by 50 km at the Wouri estuary (9.34-9.86 E, 3.89-4.34 N). The Kamerun page says only that a trading post 'was established in 1868 by the Hamburg trading company C. Woermann', the first German trading post in the Duala area, and gives no area or boundary for the post (its infobox areas, 495,000 km2 in 1910 and 790,000 km2 in 1912, are the later German colony's, years in which this row has no shape); the Douala page says nothing about 1868-1870. The extent is Cliopatria's and unverified: the pages support a trading post, not a territory of this size. Kept as the shape of record.

The same 1,897.5 km2 patch for 1870. Neither page mentions 1869 or 1870; the Kamerun page names 1868, 1874 (the founding of Jantzen & Thormählen: 'In 1874, together with the Woermann agent in Liberia') and the protectorate of 17 August 1884. Kept as Cliopatria's, unverified.

region.text: the Duala area on the Wouri estuary, where the first German trading post was established

ledger.note: 1868: the Hamburg firm C. Woermann opens the first German trading post in the Duala area. The page: it 'was established in 1868 by the Hamburg trading company C. Woermann'. The year is the page's; the region is the Cliopatria patch for the Duala area, which the page does not draw. A trading post, not a state: the page also says 'The Cameroon territory was under the informal control of the British Empire throughout the years preceding 1884'.

region.text: the Duala trading-post patch, carried on in Cliopatria's German Africa row from 1871

ledger.note: 1870: Cliopatria's Kamerun row ends and the same patch continues in its German Africa row from 1871. The Kamerun page is silent on 1870; it dates the protectorate to 17 August 1884 and names the 1874 founding of Jantzen & Thormählen. The end year is Cliopatria's, bridged.

certainty.note: A trading post: neither page gives a boundary, an area or a treaty line.

notes: kamerun (af-08-b), two pages opened (Kamerun, Douala), none failed. Cliopatria's Kamerun row (1868-1870, two identical shapes of 1,897.5 km2 at the Wouri estuary) is a trading post, not a state: the only fact the pages give is the Woermann post of 1868. German Africa's shape for 1871-1884 is the same patch (1,897.5 km2), so the post is drawn continuously from 1868 to 1884; the pages date the 1884 protectorate (17 August) but not why Cliopatria changes row in 1871. Type 'colony' and family 'germany' are the nearest fits; a reviewer may prefer to merge this dossier into german-africa as its first phase. No capital existed; the dot is the post. No wars. Gazetteer: no new names (Douala is a Natural Earth place).
